rows.description: A young professional says I would like to finish my point, then continues calmly. A steady, non-angry reclaiming holds the floor without a fight.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A toddler sits quietly on a parent's lap watching the world, content. Shared silence at this age communicates safety, not absence of connection.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A child ignored by a parent or a friend after a mistake feels intense distress, as being cut off is felt as danger. Silence used to punish teaches fear, not understanding.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager who says nothing when questioned may be defending privacy or hiding hurt. Pressing harder rarely works, while offering to talk later with no conditions often does.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 23–26

rows.description: A person waits after a proposal instead of rushing to fill the gap and finds the other side reveals more. Silence can give thinking room, but used aggressively it becomes pressure.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A person stays beside a suffering friend without speaking, offering presence only. Not rushing to fill the quiet shows that the friend's feelings can be borne.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17
